title: Blood Donation in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin has 14 fixed donation centres from five operators:** six Haema centres, two at the Charité, two Red Cross (DRK) sites and four plasma-only centres run by CSL Plasma and Octapharma.

**Pay depends on the operator.** Haema pays 20 euros for whole blood and 25 euros for plasma, the Charité 20 euros for whole blood plus a 10 euro bonus after four donations, and the Red Cross nothing for whole blood. CSL and Octapharma pay for plasma but publish no figure.
**Whole blood: at least 8 weeks apart, 6 times a year for men and 4 for women.** Haema and the Charité space women 12 weeks apart.
**Plasma: two free days between donations and up to 60 a year** under the guideline; the Charité caps its own donors at 45. Platelets: 14 days apart, up to 26 a year.
**Four of the five operators require German** in the questionnaire and the doctor's talk, and the Charité says interpreters are not allowed. CSL does not say, so call first.
**No fixed centre opens on Sunday.** On Saturday only CSL (both sites) and Octapharma Köpenick take donors; DRK mobile drives add whole-blood dates across the city.
**One simple move: choose your free day first,** then use the map to see which centres take what you want to give and when your next slot opens.
